features.name: Unique customer identity (documento) across active and disabled records
features.description: Owner report: clientes can currently be created repeatedly with the same documento (DNI). Make the customer documento unique, including against disabled (inactive) clientes, and stop a new record from silently reusing identity data already held by a disabled record. Telefono and email must stay non-unique and freely shareable. The planner must confirm whether Usuarios can express identity duplication at all (the table currently stores only username/password/activo) and record the finding instead of inventing personal-data columns.

acceptance_criteria.description: Creating a cliente with a documento already used by an active cliente is rejected with a business message that names the existing record; a distinct documento still creates the cliente.
A disabled (inactive) cliente keeps reserving its documento: creating a new cliente with that documento is rejected, while editing the disabled record itself stays possible.
Editing a cliente to a documento owned by another record is rejected, and saving its own unchanged documento still succeeds.
Telefono and email remain non-unique: two clientes may share the same phone and the same email.
Uniqueness is enforced on the persistence path (idempotent unique index or equivalent guard that also tolerates pre-existing duplicates) and validated in the service; no form contains direct SQL.

User administration does not silently accept data that a disabled user already holds: the admin sees a clear business message instead of a raw database error, or the finding is recorded as already covered with evidence.

Rule required by the owner: once an original order has warranty re-entries created it can only be inspected as it ended; it must not be re-entered, have its delivery cancelled or be edited, and the only remaining action is opening warranty re-entries (still one open at a time per feat-009). acceptance_criteria.description: With at least one warranty re-entry created for a delivered original order, cancelling that delivery is refused with a business message and writes nothing: the state/result, the Entregas rows, the Garantias rows and the audit history stay exactly as delivered.

The same frozen original order refuses every other mutation - order data edits, diagnosis, budget emission or annulment, repair start or finish, test registration or finalization, delivery or re-delivery and state transitions - with a business message and no partial write.

The restriction is enforced in the application path and in the persistence paths that can bypass it - the delivery-cancellation transaction, the order state-transition batch and the warranty re-entry creation - so a mutating call that does not come from the form is still refused and writes nothing; the remaining repositories stay reachable only through the guarded service methods.

The frozen order stays inspectable - header, history, budgets, repairs, tests, delivery and the warranty re-entry list - and opening another warranty re-entry remains allowed under the feat-009 single-open rule.
Orders without any warranty re-entry keep the previous behaviour: a delivered order can still have its delivery cancelled (ENT-03) and follow the current rules.
